## Q1
Arrange the following applet life cycle methods in sequence.

A. start()<br>
B. paint()<br>
C. init()<br>
D. stop()

## Q1 - Options
(A) A, B, C, D
(B) C, A, B, D
(C) A, C, B, D
(D) B, A, C, D

## Q1 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** Web Programming (HTML, XML, Java, Servlets)
**Source:** UGC NET Jan 2026 (2 Jan, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q82

An applet's lifecycle begins when it is loaded and ends when the browser leaves or reloads the page, and the JVM calls its lifecycle methods in a fixed order.

init() runs first, setting up the applet's initial state when it is loaded.<br>
start() runs next, beginning or resuming the applet's execution right after initialization.<br>
paint() then renders the applet's visual output on screen.<br>
stop() runs last, when the applet becomes inactive, such as when the browser navigates away from the page.

The resulting order is init() → start() → paint() → stop(), which is C, A, B, D.

## Q2
*Editorially repaired version of an ambiguous NTA item.* Consider these XML statements:

A. XML has no predefined tag set, and users can define their own tags.<br>
B. XML is used primarily for presentation.<br>
C. XML is case-sensitive.<br>
D. XML supports dynamic data representation.

Which statements are true?

## Q2 - Options
(A) B, C, and D only
(B) A, B, and D only
(C) A, C, and D only
(D) B and D only

## Q2 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** Web Programming (HTML, XML, Java, Servlets)
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2025 (26 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q60

XML has no fixed, predefined vocabulary, so applications may define their own element names. XML names are case-sensitive, and XML can represent data whose values or structure change over time. XML itself is not a presentation language; presentation is normally handled by CSS, XSLT, or another rendering layer. Thus A, C, and D are true.

## Q4
Suppose that a corporate website appearance varies according to the department that owns various documents. All the documents need to follow the corporate look and feel. The HR department does not need a separate style sheet. It needs only the sheet containing the difference from the corporate sheet.

Which of the following statements justify the above scenario?

A. The styles sheets cannot stack on each other<br>
B. The style sheets can stack on each other<br>
C. The style sheets can override each other<br>
D. The style sheets cannot override each other

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

## Q4 - Options
(A) A, C Only
(B) B, C Only
(C) B, D only
(D) A, D only

## Q4 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** Web Programming (HTML, XML, Java, Servlets)
**Source:** UGC NET Mar 2023 (15 Mar, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q47

The scenario describes exactly how CSS cascading works. The HR department's sheet layers on top of the corporate sheet, only needing to specify the differences.

Style sheets can stack on each other, meaning a page can apply multiple linked style sheets together, which lets the HR sheet build on the corporate one instead of duplicating it.

Style sheets can also override each other, so where the HR sheet defines a rule, it takes precedence over the corporate sheet's matching rule while everything else the HR sheet does not touch still applies from the corporate sheet.

This stacking and overriding behavior is the reason the HR department only needs a sheet for its differences, which matches statements B and C, not the two statements that deny stacking or overriding are possible.

## Q5
Which one of the following allows the session to continue?

## Q5 - Options
(A) When a user quits a browser
(B) When the user logs out and is invalidated by the servlet
(C) When the session is timed out due to inactivity
(D) When the user refreshes the browser and there is a persistent cookie

## Q5 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** Web Programming (HTML, XML, Java, Servlets)
**Source:** UGC NET Mar 2023 (11 Mar, Shift 2) · Paper 2 · Q12

A session ends when its cookie is lost, when the server explicitly invalidates it, or when it times out — all three of the other options describe exactly those endings.

A persistent cookie survives a page refresh because it is stored on disk rather than only in browser memory, so the browser resends the same session identifier on the next request and the server matches it back to the still-active session.

## Q6
Which of the following lists defined in HTML share similar elements?

A. Unordered lists<br>
B. Ordered lists<br>
C. Definition Lists<br>
D. Correlated lists<br>
E. Enumerated lists

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

## Q6 - Options
(A) A, B, D only
(B) A, C, E only
(C) A, B, C only
(D) A, C, D only

## Q6 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** Web Programming (HTML, XML, Java, Servlets)
**Source:** UGC NET Mar 2023 (11 Mar, Shift 2) · Paper 2 · Q47

HTML actually defines exactly three list types, because unordered lists (`<ul>`), ordered lists (`<ol>`), and definition lists (`<dl>`) are the only standard list elements in the HTML specification.

"Correlated lists" and "enumerated lists" are not real HTML elements, so they cannot belong to the group of genuine HTML list types.

A, B, and C are the three actual HTML list categories.

NTA's official final answer key for this exact sitting marked this question as dropped (full marks awarded to all candidates), consistent with the genuine interpretive ambiguity in what "share similar elements" was intended to mean here.

## Q7
Which mechanism in XML allows organizations to specify globally unique names as element tags in documents?

## Q7 - Options
(A) root
(B) header
(C) schema
(D) namespace

## Q7 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** Web Programming (HTML, XML, Java, Servlets)
**Source:** UGC NET Oct 2022 (8 Oct, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q21

An XML namespace binds a URI to a prefix, and that URI guarantees the element and attribute names using that prefix are globally unique even when documents from different organizations reuse the same tag names, avoiding naming collisions when documents are combined.

## Q12
Java Virtual Machine (JVM) is used to execute architectural neutral byte code. Which of the following is needed by the JVM for execution of Java Code?

## Q12 - Options
(A) Class loader only
(B) Class loader and Java Interpreter
(C) Class loader, Java Interpreter and API
(D) Java Interpreter only

## Q12 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** Web Programming (HTML, XML, Java, Servlets)
**Source:** UGC NET Dec 2019 (4 Dec, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q54

Running Java bytecode on the JVM requires three essential runtime components:

1. Class Loader Subsystem — dynamically loads, links, and initializes compiled class files into memory.
2. Execution Engine (Java Interpreter / JIT Compiler) — reads bytecode instructions and executes them natively on the host processor.
3. Java Core API Runtime Libraries — provides core runtime classes, system calls, and utility packages required during program execution.

Because all three components are essential, option C is correct.

## Q15
Which of the following statements is/are true?

P: An XML document with correct syntax as specified by W3C is called "Well Formed".<br>
Q: An XML documented validated against a DTD is both "Well formed" and "Valid".<br>
R: &lt;?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"&gt; is syntactly correct declaration for the version of an XML document.

Select the correct answer from the options given below:

## Q15 - Options
(A) P and Q only
(B) P and R only
(C) Q and R only
(D) All of P, Q and R

## Q15 - Hint
**Answer:** A
**Topic:** Web Programming (HTML, XML, Java, Servlets)
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2019 (24 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q5

Evaluating the statements regarding XML specifications:

- **P** is true because any XML document adhering to fundamental W3C syntax rules (proper nesting, matching tags, unique root element) is classified as well-formed.
- **Q** is true because an XML document validated against a Document Type Definition (DTD) must be well-formed before it can satisfy validity constraints.
- **R** is false because an XML declaration is a processing instruction that must terminate with `?>` rather than just `>`. The valid syntax requires `<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>`.

## Q16
Which of the following statements is/are true?

P: In a scripting language like JavaScript, types are typically associated with values, not variables.<br>
Q: It is not possible to show images on a web page without the &lt;img&gt; tag of HTML.

Select the correct answer from the options given below:

## Q16 - Options
(A) P only
(B) Q only
(C) Both P and Q
(D) Neither P nor Q

## Q16 - Hint
**Answer:** A
**Topic:** Web Programming (HTML, XML, Java, Servlets)
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2019 (24 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q78

Evaluating programming language and web presentation principles:

- **P** is true because JavaScript is dynamically typed. Variables hold references to values of any type, and type definitions attach dynamically to the runtime values themselves.
- **Q** is false because images can be displayed without `<img>` tags through CSS background-image properties, SVG graphics, HTML5 `<canvas>`, `<picture>`, or embedded data URIs.

Only statement P is true.
